sanma.title: Sanma (3 players)
sanma.intro: With 3 players, han, fu and the basic points are the same. Only who pays on **Tsumo** changes.
sanma.ron: **Ron:** same as with 4 players. The discarder pays it all.
sanma.tsumoSon: **Tsumo-son** (the most common): each of the 2 pays the usual amount and the North share is lost. A non-dealer Mangan tsumo is 4,000 + 2,000 = 6,000 instead of 8,000.
sanma.split: **North split:** the North share is split between the 2, rounded up to the next hundred. The same Mangan becomes 5,000 + 3,000 = 8,000.
sanma.honba: **Honba:** on Ron, 300 per honba. On Tsumo, each payer adds 100 per honba, so the winner gets 200 (with Basengo, 1,500 and 500).
sanma.kita: **Kita:** each North set aside is 1 dora (nukidora). It counts in han like any dora.
sanma.tip: In the calculator, pick 3 players to see the total received on Tsumo.

hanFuTutorial.title: How to count Han and Fu

overview.title: Overview
overview.intro: A hand's value depends on two numbers: han, which measures the strength of the yaku and dora, and fu, which counts the details of how the hand was built and completed.
overview.step2: **5 or more**? It's a limit hand and you don't need to count fu.
overview.step4: With han and fu, **look up the table**.

han.title: Counting han
han.sum: Add up the han of every yaku in the hand.
han.dora: Each dora adds 1 han, but dora is not a yaku: without a yaku you cannot win.
han.open: Some yaku are worth 1 han less with an open hand.
han.reading: If the hand can be read in more than one way, the reading with more han counts.

baseFu.title: Base fu
baseFu.futei: Every hand starts with **20 fu** (fūtei), whatever its yaku.
baseFu.chiitoitsu: Chiitoitsu (seven pairs): always a fixed **25 fu**, nothing added and no rounding.

sets.title: Fu from sets
sets.intro: Each triplet and each kan adds fu; sequences add nothing.
sets.tip: Closed doubles, terminal or honor doubles again, and a kan is worth 4 times the triplet.

pairWait.title: Pair, wait and rounding
pairWait.pair: The pair only adds fu when it is of a tile that would give han as a triplet. Not just any wind: only yours and the round's.
pairWait.pairWind: A value wind, **yours** (your seat) or the **round** wind: **+2**.
pairWait.pairDouble: If it is both at once (e.g. you are East in the East round): **+2** under the default rule, or **+4** with the Double wind pair rule on. Never more than that.
pairWait.wait: Waiting on a single tile: **+2**. Applies to a pair wait, a middle wait (4-6 waiting on 5) or an edge wait (1-2 waiting on 3).
pairWait.openHand: An open hand left with only the 20 base fu becomes **30**.
pairWait.round: Round the total up to the next ten (e.g. 34 → **40**).

points.title: From Han/Fu to points
points.intro: The Quick table already does this math for you. But if you want to understand where the values come from, this is the formula. So:
points.ron: **Ron:** a non-dealer receives 4× the basic points and the dealer 6×, all from whoever discarded.
points.tsumo: **Tsumo:** the dealer receives 2× from each player. A non-dealer receives 2× from the dealer and 1× from each of the others.
points.round: Round each payment up to the next hundred.
points.cap: If the basic points go over 2,000, they are capped at 2,000 (Mangan).
points.exampleCap: It went over 2,000, so it is capped at 2,000. It's a Mangan.
points.mathIntro: Nobody needs to do 110 × 64 in their head. There are shortcuts.
points.double: Raising 2 to a power is just doubling. 2⁶ = double 6 times.
points.split: Split 110 into 100 + 10, which are easy to multiply.
points.eleven: 110 is 11 × 10. Multiplying by 11 is easy: add the two digits and put the sum in the middle.
points.lines: A popular visual method, known as Japanese multiplication.
points.linesLabel: 11 × 64 with lines: the crossings give 6 on the left, 6 + 4 = 10 in the middle and 4 on the right.
points.payment: Multiplying by 4 is doubling twice. By 6 is the 4 plus the 2.
points.finalTip: Went over 2,000 basic points? You can stop counting. It's a Mangan.
points.curiosity: In Japan, the multiplication table is memorized as a chant called kuku (九九). Experienced mahjong players do the same with the score table: after a while you don't calculate, you remember.

limits.title: Limit hands
limits.mangan: Mangan|5 han, or 4 han 40+ fu, or 3 han 70+ fu|8,000|12,000
limits.kiriage: Some rule sets round 4 han 30 fu and 3 han 60 fu up to Mangan (Kiriage Mangan). In the app, this option is in the Scoring rules of the Hand Calculator; the Quick table shows the values without it.

honba.title: Honba
honba.text: Each honba adds 300 points for the winner. On ron, the discarder pays the 300. On tsumo, each player pays 100.

victory.tsumo: You completed the hand with a tile drawn from the wall. All other players pay.
victory.ron: You completed the hand with a tile discarded by another player. Only the discarder pays.
victory.menzen: With a closed hand, tsumo is worth 1 han (Menzen Tsumo) and is a yaku, so on its own it already makes your hand valid.
victory.yaku: A scoring condition that lets you win. Every hand needs at least one.

demo.fourthAka: With three regular 5s in the hand, the 5 on the keyboard is already the red one

honba.counter: Counter of extra rounds. It goes up when the dealer wins or when the round ends in a draw.
honba.points: Each honba adds 300 points to the winner. On tsumo, each player pays 100. On ron, the discarder pays 300.
honba.basengo: At some tables, each honba is worth 1,500 points instead of 300. On tsumo, each player pays 500 per honba. To use it, turn on Basengo in Scoring rules, under the sliders icon ([[engrenagem]]) of the Hand Calculator.

dora.title: Which tile is the Dora?
dora.inHand: Enter how many dora you have in your hand.
dora.indicators: Select the dora indicators. The indicator is not the dora. It determines which tile counts as dora.
dora.uraDora: The tile under each dora indicator in the dead wall. It works as one more dora indicator, but is only revealed to whoever wins after declaring Riichi.
dora.aka: The red fives count as dora, 1 han each. To use them, turn on Aka dora in Scoring rules, under the sliders icon ([[engrenagem]]) of the Hand Calculator.
dora.flaming: When the dora indicator is a red 5, each dora from that indicator is worth 2 han. To use it, turn on Aka dora and Flaming dora in Scoring rules, under the sliders icon ([[engrenagem]]) of the Hand Calculator.
dora.curiosity: In Riichi Mahjong, the word dora (ドラ) is short for “dragon”, which in Japanese is pronounced doragon (ドラゴン).
dora.dragonPrince: That's why they say whoever never gives up their dora is a prince (or princess) of dragons.

furiten.rule: In furiten you cannot win by ron, only by tsumo. Declaring ron in furiten is chombo.
furiten.discards: A tile that would complete your hand is among your own discards. It lasts as long as your wait includes that tile.
furiten.temporary: You let a tile that would complete your hand go by without declaring ron. It lasts until your next discard.
furiten.riichi: After declaring Riichi, you let a tile that would complete your hand go by. It lasts until the end of the round, because the hand can no longer change.
furiten.register: Record your discards here, because that is how the app checks furiten. Temporary and Riichi furiten depend on what happened at the table and are not checked.

seatWind.seat: The wind of your seat this round. A triplet of your wind is worth 1 han and is a yaku, so on its own it already makes your hand valid.
seatWind.dealer: Whoever sits East is the dealer (oya) and receives 1.5× the points when winning.

roundWind.round: The wind of the current round. It is East in the first half of the game and South in the second. A triplet of the round wind is also worth 1 han and is a yaku.
roundWind.double: If the round wind is also your wind, the triplet is worth 2 han.

riichi.declaration: A declaration made with a closed hand one step away from completion (tenpai). It costs a 1,000-point bet.
riichi.value: Worth 1 han and is a yaku, so on its own it already makes your hand valid. It also unlocks ura-dora. After declaring, you can no longer change your hand.
riichi.doubleRiichi: Riichi declared on the first discard, with no calls before it. Worth 2 han instead of 1 and is also a yaku.
riichi.ippatsu: Winning within one go-around after Riichi, with no calls in between. Worth +1 han. It is a yaku, but only exists together with Riichi.
riichi.uraDora: The tile under each dora indicator in the dead wall. It works as one more dora indicator, but is only revealed to whoever wins after declaring Riichi.

specialConditions.allYaku: They are all yaku, so any of them already makes your hand valid, even without another yaku.
specialConditions.tenhouChiihou: Winning with the starting hand. Tenhou is the dealer's and Chiihou the other players'. They are worth Yakuman.
specialConditions.rinshan: Winning with the tile drawn after a kan. Worth +1 han.
specialConditions.chankan: Ron on the tile another player added to a pon to make a kan. Worth +1 han.
specialConditions.haitei: Winning by tsumo with the last tile of the wall. Worth +1 han.
specialConditions.houtei: Winning by ron on the last discard of the hand. Worth +1 han.

notation.intro: Write the tile numbers followed by the suit: m (Man), p (Pin), s (Sou) and z (honors). Several numbers before the same suit all belong to it: 2388m447p is 2, 3, 8 and 8 of Man and 4, 4 and 7 of Pin.
notation.honors: 1z to 4z are the East, South, West and North winds; 5z, 6z and 7z are the white, green and red dragons.
notation.aka: Use 0 instead of 5: 0m, 0p and 0s are the red fives (Aka dora).
notation.win: The last tile of the closed hand is the winning tile, the one that completed the hand. In 123456m789p1122z, the winning tile is 2z.
notation.tip: You can build several groups and numbers and tap the suit only at the end; it applies to all of them, which is handy for Honitsu and Itsu. Each number shows below it the honor it becomes with z. AC clears everything. To go back to the tile keyboard, tap Tiles or swipe your finger to the right.
notation.chi: A run of 3 in the same suit taken from the player before you. Type 123m and tap Chi. Or tap Chi first and then a number: pick the run (still without a suit) and tap the suit. With Chi selected, tapping a tile in the hand also makes the chi.
notation.pon: A triplet taken from any player’s discard. Type 111p and tap Pon. Or tap Pon first and then 1: three blank 1s wait for the suit; tap p.
notation.kan: 4 of a kind, the 4th taken from another player’s discard. Type 1111s and tap Kan. Or tap Kan first and then 1: four 1s appear; tap s.
notation.closedKan: 4 of a kind, all from your own hand. Type 7777z and tap Closed kan. Or tap Closed kan first and then 7: four 7s appear; tap z.
notation.display: With a physical keyboard, a call is a letter at the end of the group: c for Chi, Pon and Kan (123mc, 111pc, 1111sc) and a for Closed kan (7777za).

tiles.title: Building the hand
tiles.intro: Tap the tiles on the keyboard to build the hand, in any order: the app sorts it for you. To remove a tile, tap it in the hand.
tiles.win: Unlike other calculators, you don’t have to leave the winning tile for last. The last tile you tap becomes the winning tile, but with a complete hand you can change it in Change winning tile and pick any tile in the hand.
tiles.waits: With 13 tiles, the keyboard shows above each wait how many han the hand is worth winning on it. Dimmed tiles don’t complete the hand.
tiles.chi: Tap Chi and then a tile. If it makes more than one sequence, the options show up in Choose the Chi: tap the right one. With Chi selected, tapping a tile in the hand also makes the chi with the tiles already there.
tiles.pon: Tap Pon and then the tile. All three go in as a Pon, using the ones already in the hand.
tiles.kan: Tap Kan and then the tile. All four go in as an Open kan.
tiles.closedKan: Tap Closed kan and then the tile. If the hand already has three or four of it, they become the Kan.
tiles.aka: With Aka dora on in the rules [[engrenagem]], hold the 5 to add the red 5 when the phone is upright. The red dot in the corner of the 5 shows the red one is still free. With the phone sideways, on tablets and on computers, the red 5 is the last tile of each suit. Each suit has only one: the fourth 5 of a suit is always the red one, in a Kan too.
tiles.akaHan: With 13 tiles, the badge on the 5 shows both values: first the han winning on the regular 5 and, in red, winning on the red 5. In 7/8 HAN, the regular 5 gives 7 and the red one gives 8, because of Aka dora.
tiles.guide: The cap opens the Pocket guide: Yaku with examples, terms and tables to check during the game.
tiles.finish: With a complete hand, Finish hand takes you to the win options: ron or tsumo, winds, Riichi, doras and honba. Each part there has its own ?.
tiles.tip: Rather type? MPSZ swaps the tile keyboard for notation, like 123m. To go back, tap Tiles.

rulesModal.help: Choose the variations used at your table.

akadora.title: Aka dora
akadora.help: Counts the red fives as dora. When on, the keyboard shows a red 5 for each suit.

doraFlamejante.title: Flaming dora
doraFlamejante.help: When the dora indicator is a red 5, each dora is worth 2 han. Requires Aka dora.

tanyaoAberto.title: Open Tanyao
tanyaoAberto.help: Whether Tanyao counts with open calls. Common in modern Japanese rules, but some groups play kuitan nashi.

fuVentosDuplo.title: Double wind pair
fuVentosDuplo.help: When the pair is both the round and the seat wind, some rules add 4 fu. In modern competitive rules it is usually 2 fu.

fuRinshan.title: Fu on Rinshan
fuRinshan.help: Whether a Rinshan Kaihou win also gets the 2 tsumo fu.

kiriageMangan.title: Kiriage Mangan
kiriageMangan.help: Rounds 4 han 30 fu and 3 han 60 fu up to Mangan when the table plays kiriage.

kazoeYakuman.title: Kazoe Yakuman
kazoeYakuman.help: Whether 13 or more han without a natural Yakuman count as a counted Yakuman or stop at Sanbaiman.

yakumanDuplo.title: Double Yakuman
yakumanDuplo.help: Lets special forms such as Suuankou tanki or 13-wait Kokushi be worth double Yakuman.

multiYakuman.title: Stacked Yakuman
multiYakuman.help: Lets multiple Yakuman add up in the same hand, for example Daisuushii together with Tsuuiisou.

basengo.title: Basengo
basengo.help: Each honba is worth 1,500 points instead of 300. On tsumo, each player pays 500 per honba.

chomboMangan.title: Chombo penalty
chomboMangan.help: How much a player who commits chombo pays (no yaku, ron in furiten). Mangan: 8,000 (12,000 as East). Yakuman: 32,000 (48,000 as East).

tableConfig.nagashiManganHelp: On an exhaustive draw, a player who discarded only terminals and honors, with none of those discards called, is paid like a Mangan tsumo.
tableConfig.abortiveDrawsHelp: The hand ends with no payments: the dealer stays, the honba goes up and the sticks stay on the table.
tableConfig.abortiveNineTerminalsHelp: On the first draw, with no calls at the table, a player holding 9 or more kinds of terminals and honors may end the hand.
tableConfig.abortiveFourWindsHelp: In the first go-around, with no calls, all 4 players discard the same wind.
tableConfig.abortiveFourKansHelp: Different players declare 4 kans in the same hand. If one player made all 4, the hand goes on.
tableConfig.abortiveFourRiichiHelp: All 4 players declare Riichi in the same hand.
tableConfig.okaOffHelp: With no oka, the return equals the starting points: nobody gets an extra prize and the final total is zero.
tableConfig.umaInvalid: Each row must add up to zero and never rise from 1st to 4th.
tableConfig.umaFloatNote: Above means finishing with points equal to or higher than the return. With all 4 above, the None above row applies.
tableConfig.umaFloatHelp: Floating: the uma changes with how many players finished above the return.
tableConfig.umaFloatCurrent: With the current points, this row applies: {{line}}.
tableConfig.leftoverSticks: Riichi sticks left at the end
tableConfig.ronTripleAborts: Double ron; triple is an abortive draw
tableConfig.tobiHelp: The game ends when someone goes below zero.
tableConfig.agariYameHelp: A dealer in 1st place on the last hand may end the game.
tableConfig.extraRoundHelp: Goes on to South or West if nobody reached the extension target.
tableConfig.extensionTargetHelp: At the end of the last round, if nobody has these points, the game goes on until someone gets there. It is separate from the return, so it also works without oka.
tableConfig.customNote: Values changed: the set is now Custom. Tap a set to go back to it.
tableConfig.okaHelp: Extra prize for 1st place. It is the difference between return and starting points, times 4.
tableConfig.umaHelp: Bonus or penalty by placement, in thousands of points. The 4 must add up to zero.
tableConfig.leftoverHelp: Riichi sticks nobody won by the end of the game. They can go to 1st place or be discarded.
tableConfig.returnHelp1: The reference value for the final score. At the end of the game, each player's points are compared with the return, then the uma for their placement is added.
tableConfig.returnHelp2: If the return is higher than the starting points, the difference from all players becomes the **oka**, an extra prize for 1st place.

guide.intro: Leave the phone in the middle of the table, with 東 facing the dealer. Each plate shows the wind of whoever sits there and the dice totals that open the wall in front of them.
guide.timer: The 30 s timer is on by default. On your turn, tap the plate of your wind and the time starts again from full in the center. Since Pon, Chi and Kan skip players, the timer doesn’t guess whose turn it is: whoever plays next taps. If time runs out, the center blinks and the alarm sounds.
guide.actions: Tapping anywhere on the table outside the plates, the center included, opens the actions: next round, honba, dice, Wind Draw, restart from 東1 and the timer length.
guide.dealer: Next round passes 東 to the next player. Turn the phone so 東 keeps facing the dealer. The table follows the phone even if the screen rotates by itself, but the header and the bar switch sides. To avoid that, lock rotation in the phone settings.
guide.honba: When the dealer wins or the round is a draw, tap + on honba: the number goes up and the hand restarts with the same dealer. The − fixes an extra tap.
guide.screen: The screen stays on while this table is open, when the device allows it.
